The Challenge of Reservoir Uncertainty

Traditional seismic interpretation delivers maps and cross-sections, but often fails to answer the critical question: how confident should we be in these results?

Drilling decisions involve significant capital allocation. Without rigorous uncertainty quantification, organizations either over-invest in low-confidence opportunities or under-value high-confidence prospects.

Single-Answer Interpretations

Deterministic results hide the range of possibilities consistent with the data.

Disconnected Workflows

Processing, inversion, and interpretation often treated as separate steps without integrated uncertainty propagation.

Qualitative Confidence

"High," "medium," "low" confidence labels without quantitative basis or reproducibility.

The CONFIRM Difference

Quantified Confidence Intervals

Every property estimate includes statistically rigorous uncertainty bounds.

Integrated Workflow

Uncertainty tracked from seismic data through to final reservoir properties.

Auditable Results

Transparent methodology that can be reviewed and validated.

The CONFIRM Methodology

CONFIRM integrates five interconnected components, each grounded in established geoscience principles, with uncertainty propagated systematically through the entire workflow.

1

Data Integration

Systematic compilation of well logs, seismic data, and geological knowledge with quality assessment.

Scientific Basis: Data quality metrics, measurement uncertainty characterization
2

Rock Physics Calibration

Establish quantitative relationships between reservoir properties and elastic response using well data.

Scientific Basis: Gassmann theory, contact mechanics, empirical calibration with scatter quantification
3

Seismic Inversion

Transform seismic amplitudes to elastic properties using deterministic and/or stochastic methods.

Scientific Basis: Convolutional model, Zoeppritz equations, Bayesian inference
4

Property Estimation

Convert elastic properties to reservoir properties using calibrated rock physics transforms.

Scientific Basis: Calibrated transforms with regression uncertainty, Monte Carlo propagation
5

Confidence Mapping

Generate property maps with associated confidence intervals and probability of meeting thresholds.

Scientific Basis: Error propagation theory, probabilistic mapping, decision analysis

Scientific Foundation

CONFIRM is not a black box. Every step is based on established physics and mathematics that can be examined, validated, and reproduced.

Theoretical Framework

Built on Gassmann fluid substitution theory (1951), Biot poroelasticity (1956), and Hertz-Mindlin contact mechanics - equations that have been validated through decades of laboratory and field observations.

Statistical Rigor

Uncertainty quantification follows established statistical methods: Bayesian inference for combining prior knowledge with observations, Monte Carlo simulation for error propagation, and cross-validation for model testing.

Calibration Requirements

We explicitly require well control for calibration. CONFIRM does not claim to predict properties without ground truth - it provides a rigorous framework for extending well observations to undrilled areas with quantified confidence.

CONFIRM Deliverables

Decision-ready outputs designed for integration into exploration and development workflows.

Property Maps with Confidence

Porosity, net pay, and lithology maps accompanied by standard deviation or percentile bounds at each location.

Probability of Success Maps

Probability that properties exceed economic thresholds (e.g., P(porosity > 15%) at each map location.

Rock Physics Templates

Calibrated crossplots showing expected elastic property ranges for different lithologies and fluids.

Sensitivity Analysis Report

Documentation of which uncertainties contribute most to final property uncertainty, identifying where additional data would be most valuable.

Methodology Documentation

Complete documentation of all assumptions, parameters, and algorithms used - enabling internal review and audit.

Integration Support

Results delivered in standard formats (SEGY, ASCII, Petrel-compatible) with support for integration into your reservoir modeling workflow.
